verdicts.why: Held: minor employer. Beck's job on a Wonder Studios effects crew is a single past job, told and seen in episode 5 only. The Marvel Database episode page names it as Beck's address. Whether a minor job like this counts is an open owner question, so the record stays as it is.

Episode 16 tells it: after he was expelled, his parents enlisted Morrie in the navy, and he was in its special research unit when he went overboard and mutated. The Marvel Database lists the US Navy as mentioned. Navy service is an armed force, not a minor job. Nothing on screen discharges him, so U.S. Navy stays as his stage.

Episode 35: Alistair breaks the Kingpin's programming on finding his father frozen and turns on him (Marvel Database: 'Having defected from the Kingpin once and for all', with the Kingpin listed as a former employer). By episode 46 he is Silvermane's top scientist. The departure in between is missing, so the Independent stage and the left are right.

Marko's Army service is his past: a WWI soldier captured in the Meuse-Argonne offensive and experimented on, told in episode 5. He works for Silvermane in the present, from episode 1 on. The past group goes first. Silvermane dies in episode 8 and Flint leaves with Cat, so the Independent end and the left stand.

Gangland (ep 23) tells it, and both wikis say the same: he was a Silvermane enforcer who dated Sable and was fired before he joined Tombstone. Tombstone then fires him at the summit and he goes into hiding, so he ends the show in no group. 'Silvermane's Mob' is the name the dataset already uses for this Silvermane and Sable. The Tombstone stage stays held, and if the owner names it, it goes between these two.

Eddie works in Connors's ESU lab from his first episode, where Peter and Gwen intern. He loses the job when Black Cat tries to steal the symbiote he was meant to guard, and Debra Whitman is his replacement. He only visits later to steal the gene cleanser and is never rehired. This is a real workplace across several episodes, not a single minor job, and the form matches Connors's record.

She already leads her own band of outcasts (filed as The Omegas) when Magneto finds her, and she and her gang then ally with Magneto's Brotherhood. She is never in the Brotherhood before her gang, so the opening Brotherhood stage is wrong. The Void variant fights for Cassandra Nova, whose group has no on-screen name, so it adds no stage.

Night of the Sentinels shows Gyrich's agency (the record's 'Mutant Control Agency', as on Gyrich) behind the Sentinels and feeding them its mutant files, and the Sentinels guard its headquarters. The agency is shut down after the raid. In episode 13 Master Mold and its Sentinels turn on their makers. In X-Men '97 S1 episode 10, Bastion falls and OZT ends (Defunct). The Prime Sentinels' humanity is restored, so both departures hold.

In the final fight, Fisk admits he killed Jack Murdock on Fallon's orders. Wikipedia's cast notes say Fallon 'once employed Fisk as a hitman'. That is a past group the screen tells, so it goes first under the dataset's name 'Fallon's Mob', as on Jack Murdock.

S1E1: Schmidt heads HYDRA as Hitler's science division. Hitler sends Roeder to summon him to Berlin, and Schmidt says 'A god does not answer to a man', shoots Roeder and declares the Third Reich will fall and HYDRA will rise. That is service to Nazi Germany and a break from it on screen, so HYDRA is his last stage.

S2E4 (ep 13): Valkyrie defeats Topaz and melts the Grandmaster, and is crowned king of Sakaar. He is deposed, the same move the main record gives at Thor: Ragnarok, and in the mid-credits scene he is a puddle begging Topaz to collect him.

S1E4 opens with neurosurgeon Strange and Christine celebrating his successful radical hemispherectomy, and his illusion later recreates Metro-General. The MCU Wiki lists him as a former Metro-General employee. This is his real workplace, the same group his main record and Christine's variant carry, and he leaves it for Kamar-Taj, so it goes first.

The Asset: Coulson briefs that Hall is a S.H.I.E.L.D. asset, and Fitz and Simmons remember him as their second-year chemical kinetics advisor. The MCU Wiki calls him an instructor at the S.H.I.E.L.D. Academy, so he worked for S.H.I.E.L.D., which is employment, not study. Item 98 gives the full list with the departure.

The departure is right. Hall leaked his own location to Quinn to escape S.H.I.E.L.D., then turned on both of them to bury the gravitonium, telling Coulson S.H.I.E.L.D. is just as guilty. But a left needs the Independent stage it records, as in every other left in the data, so it is added after S.H.I.E.L.D.

He served in the Soviet 478th Rifle Division and was listed dead after Finow in 1944, which Dooley and Thompson find in episode 4. He joined Leviathan after the war and then betrayed it as an 'independent businessman' (episodes 1 and 2). The past army stage goes first, and the Independent end and the left stand.

Burch says on screen that the serum is 'a little concoction that he's been perfecting since his days with the SIS', so the screen tells a past MI6 service that has ended. MI6 is the dataset's name for SIS, and the MCU Wiki gives his affiliation as MI6 (formerly). It goes first, followed by the departure. Burch's gang stays held.

Wikipedia's plot calls Krieger 'a familiar, a human thrall loyal to vampires'. He serves Frost, reports to him and is killed for his failure while Frost is still in the House of Erebus. Under the familiar rule (Vreede in the House of Talos), a familiar is in his vampire master's house.
